title: The pool scenario's first record is run at the full budget and design.md states what the numbers support
goal: kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.csv holds one record of scenario pool, run on Claude Code's current version with the free scenarios always-on, retrieval, verdict and tool-speed re-run the same day: the kb arms haiku-5-5, haiku-4-5 and sonnet-5-5 and the router on every pool row at 3 reps and both effort levels, the hook arm on every row, the web arms on the 20-row subset at 2 reps, shape session on 5 groups of six at 2 reps, and an opus-5-5 sanity subset of 10 rows at 1 rep, within the spend gate's budget; kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md's pool section states the setup, the records table, the tables and what they show (tokens per right answer by kind and arm, fixed share, effort, Haiku 5.5 against 4.5, marginal input by position), each conclusion in kb/_self/design.md and kb/_self/token-efficiency.md citing the section; report --check passes and no number in README.md disagrees

gates.question: The pool record's paid runs are estimated at about 100 USD (kb arms 3 reps x 2 efforts, router, web subset, session shape, Opus subset); which spend cap does the run get?
options: cap 120 USD: the full set as the goal states
cap 70 USD: 2 reps on the kb arms, no Opus subset
cap 30 USD: haiku-5-5, haiku-4-5 and router only, 2 reps, one effort
gates.recommendation: cap 120 USD: the full set as the goal states
gates.answer: cap 120 USD: the full set as the goal states

notes: Estimate behind the gate, from the 2026-09-28 records: a kb question costs about 0.03 USD on Haiku and 0.10 on Sonnet 5.5, the router 0.01-0.03, a web question 0.01-0.20; 120 rows x 3 kb arms x 2 efforts x 3 reps is 2,160 runs at a mean near 0.04 USD, so about 85 USD, plus router (5), web subset (15), session shape (10) and the Opus subset (3): about 100-120 USD. Run order: the free scenarios first (always-on for the 2.1.290 fixed context, retrieval, verdict, tool-speed on 311 topics), then pool at one rep as a dry run that checks every row's regex fires on some arm, then the full set. Record the resolved model of each alias from the result event. A pool row whose check no arm passes at any rep is a finding for the review (a bad regex or a real miss), not a reason to edit the row mid-run. Write the design.md conclusions only from cells whose spread is below their difference, as the navigation section does. Checks before the work: report --check passes on today's tree and fails once ST-k4uqib77's pool markers are in benchmarks.md with no rows (its no-rows rule), so it proves this story's record; selfdoc.py stale pins that design.md and token-efficiency.md edits leave no doc stale, a check that must stay green. From ST-k4uqib77's operator gates (2026-10-08): g1, the pool section's bench: table markers in kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md land with this story's record (ST-k4uqib77 landed the setup text, Counting and the no-rows rule, no markers), so report --check fails only once this story adds the markers and passes when the record is in benchmarks.csv; ST-ohz5si2o's marginal-input marker lands here too. g3, the web arms' kind list covers 62 rows per arm: this run selects the 20-row web subset with run pool's --kinds and --reps flags to stay within the 120 USD cap. run pool --dry-run prints the run count before any paid run.
